And his companions said, "Thus you shall speak to the people, saying, 'My littleness is thicker than my father's waist; my father flogged you with whips, but I will rule you with scorpions.'" And the word was pleasing in the sight of Rehoboam; and he answered the people just as his companions, the young men, had counseled him. And all the people spoke as one man, each to his neighbor, and they all cried out, saying, "We have no portion in David, nor an inheritance in the son of Jesse! To your tents, Israel, for this man is not to be a ruler nor a leader!" And all the people scattered from Shechem, and each went away to his tent. And Rehoboam exerted himself, and departed and mounted his chariot and entered into Jerusalem; and the whole tribe of Judah and the whole tribe of Benjamin went after him. And it happened at the turn of the year that Rehoboam gathered every man of Judah and Benjamin, and went up to fight against Jeroboam at Shechem. And the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, a man of God: "Speak to Rehoboam king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the remnant of the people, saying, 'Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up nor fight against your brothers, the sons of Israel; return, each one to his own house, for this matter has come from Me.'" And they listened to the word of the Lord, and refrained from going, according to the word of the Lord.
verses.12:25: And Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived in it; and he went out from there and built Penuel.
verses.12:26: And Jeroboam said in his heart, "Look, now the kingdom will return to the house of David:
verses.12:27: if this people goes up to offer sacrifice in the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, then the heart of the people will turn back to the Lord and to their lord, to Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will kill me."
verses.12:28: And the king took counsel, and went and made two golden heifers, and said to the people, "Let it be enough for you to go up to Jerusalem; here are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt."
verses.12:29: And he set the one in Bethel, and the other he put in Dan.
verses.12:30: And this matter became a sin; and the people went before the one as far as Dan.
verses.12:31: And he made houses on high places, and he made priests from a part of the people who were not of the sons of Levi.
verses.12:32: And Jeroboam instituted a festival in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the festival that was in the land of Judah, and he went up to the altar that he had made in Bethel to sacrifice to the heifers that he had made, and he stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places that he had made.
verses.12:33: And he went up to the altar that he had made, on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, in the festival that he had fabricated from his own heart, and he instituted a festival for the sons of Israel. And he went up to the altar to offer sacrifice.
verses.13:1: And look, a man of God from Judah came by the word of the Lord to Bethel, and Jeroboam was standing by the altar to offer sacrifice.
verses.13:2: And he cried out to the altar by the word of the Lord, "Altar, altar, thus says the Lord: Look, a son is born to the house of David, Josiah is his name; and he will sacrifice on you the priests of the high places who offer sacrifice on you, and he will burn human bones on you."
verses.13:3: And he will give a portent on that day, saying, "This is the word that the Lord has spoken, saying, 'Look, the altar is splitting apart, and the fatness that is on it will be poured out.'"
verses.13:4: And it happened, when King Jeroboam heard the words of the man of God who had cried out against the altar that was in Bethel, that the king stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, "Seize him!" And look, his hand, which he had stretched out against him, withered, and he was not able to bring it back to himself.
verses.13:5: And the altar split apart, and the fatness was poured out from the altar according to the portent that the man of God had given by the word of the Lord.
verses.13:6: And King Jeroboam said to the man of God, "Implore your God, and let my hand return to me." And the man of God implored the face of the Lord, and He brought the king's hand back to him, and it became as before.
verses.13:7: And the king spoke to the man of God, "Come with me into the house and eat a meal, and I will give you a gift."
verses.13:8: And the man of God said to the king, "If you give me half of your house, I will not go in with you, nor will I eat bread, nor will I drink water in this place.
verses.13:9: For thus the Lord commanded me by a word, saying, 'Do not eat bread, and do not drink water, and do not return by the way on which you went.'"
verses.13:10: And he departed by another way, and did not return by the way on which he had come to Bethel.
verses.13:11: Now a certain old prophet was living in Bethel; and his sons came and recounted to him all the deeds that the man of God had done during the day in Bethel, the words that he had spoken to the king; and they turned the face of their father.
verses.13:12: And their father spoke to them, saying, "Which way has he gone?" And his sons showed him the way by which the man of God who had come from Judah went up.
verses.13:13: And he said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." So they saddled the donkey for him, and he mounted it.
verses.13:14: And he went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak, and said to him, "Are you the man of God who has come from Judah?" And he said to him, "I am."
verses.13:15: And he said to him, "Come with me and eat bread."
verses.13:16: And he said, "I cannot return with you, nor will I eat bread, nor will I drink water in this place.
verses.13:17: For thus the Lord has commanded me by a word, saying, 'Do not eat bread there, and do not drink water, and do not return there by the way on which you went.'"
verses.13:18: And he said to him, "I also am a prophet just as you are, and an angel has spoken to me by the word of the Lord, saying, 'Bring him back to yourself into your house, and let him eat bread and drink water.'" But he lied to him.
verses.13:19: And he brought him back, and he ate bread in his house and drank water.
verses.13:20: And it happened, while they were sitting, that the word of the Lord came to the prophet who had brought him back.
verses.13:21: And he said to the man of God who had come from Judah, saying, "Thus says the Lord: Because you defied the word of the Lord, and did not keep the commandment that the Lord your God commanded you,
verses.13:22: and returned, and ate bread and drank water in this place of which He spoke to you, saying, 'You must not eat bread and must not drink water,' your body will certainly not enter the tomb of your fathers."
verses.13:23: And it happened, after eating bread and drinking water, that he saddled the donkey for him, and he turned back and departed.
verses.13:24: And a lion found him on the road and put him to death; and his body was thrown on the road, and the donkey was standing beside it, and the lion was standing beside the body.
verses.13:25: And look, men were passing by, and they saw the corpse thrown on the road, and the lion was standing close beside the corpse; and they entered and spoke in the city where the old prophet was living.
verses.13:26: And the one who had brought him back from the road heard, and he said, "This is the man of God who defied the word of the Lord."
verses.13:28: And he went and found his body thrown on the road, and the donkey and the lion were standing beside the body; and the lion had not eaten the body of the man of God, and had not crushed the donkey.
verses.13:29: And the prophet lifted up the body of the man of God and placed it on the donkey, and brought him back into the city,
verses.13:30: the prophet, to bury him in his own tomb; and they mourned for him, "Alas, brother!"
verses.13:31: And it happened, after mourning for him, that he said to his sons, saying, "When I die, bury me in this tomb in which the man of God is buried; lay me beside his bones, so that my bones may be saved with his bones.
verses.13:32: For the word that he spoke by the word of the Lord against the altar in Bethel and against the high houses that are in Samaria will certainly take place."
verses.13:33: And after this matter Jeroboam did not turn back from his wickedness, and he turned again and made priests of high places from part of the people; whoever wished, he would fill his hand, and he became a priest for the high places.
verses.13:34: And this matter resulted in sin for the house of Jeroboam, and in destruction and eradication from the face of the earth.
verses.14:21: And Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned over Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the Lord had chosen from all the tribes of Israel to put His name there. And his mother's name was Maacham, an Ammonite.
verses.14:22: And Rehoboam did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, and he provoked Him to jealousy in all that their fathers had done, in their sins that they had committed.
verses.14:23: And they built for themselves high places and pillars and groves on every high hill and beneath every shady tree.
verses.14:24: And there was a conspiracy in the land, and they did some of all the abominations of the nations whom the Lord had removed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.14:25: And it happened in the fifth year of Rehoboam's reign that Shishak king of Egypt went up against Jerusalem,
verses.14:26: and he took all the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king's house, and the golden spears that David had taken from the hand of the servants of Hadarezer king of Zobah and had brought into Jerusalem, all that he took, the golden weapons.
verses.14:27: And King Rehoboam made bronze weapons in their place; and the leaders of the runners, who guarded the gateway of the king's house, set upon him.
verses.14:28: And it happened, whenever the king went into the house of the Lord, that the runners would carry them and would deposit them into the chamber of the runners.
verses.14:29: And the rest of the matters of Rehoboam and all that he did, look, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.14:30: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days.
verses.14:31: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and he was buried with his fathers in the city of David; and Abiu his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:1: And in the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abiu son of Jeroboam became king over Judah,
verses.15:2: and he reigned six years; and the name of his mother was Maacah, daughter of Absalom.
verses.15:3: And he walked in the sins of his father which he committed before him, and his heart was not complete with the Lord his God like the heart of his father.
verses.15:4: For on account of David the Lord gave him a remnant, so that He might establish his children after him and establish Jerusalem,
verses.15:5: since David did what was right before the Lord; he did not turn aside from all that He commanded him all the days of his life.
verses.15:7: And the rest of the matters of Abiu and all that he did, look, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Judah? And there was war between Abiu and Jeroboam.
verses.15:8: And Abiu slept with his fathers in the twenty-fourth year of Jeroboam, and he was buried with his fathers in the city of David; and Asa his son became king in his place.
verses.15:9: In the twenty-fourth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa became king over Judah,
verses.15:10: and he reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Ana, daughter of Absalom.
verses.15:11: And Asa did what was right before the Lord, like David his father.
verses.15:12: And he removed the initiation rites from the land, and he sent away all the practices which his fathers had done.
verses.15:13: And Ana his mother he removed from being leader, because she held an assembly in her grove; and Asa cut down her hiding places and burned them with fire in the brook of the cedars.
verses.15:14: But the high places he did not remove; yet the heart of Asa was complete with the Lord all his days.
verses.15:15: And he brought in the pillars of his father, and he brought his own pillars into the house of the Lord, of silver and gold, and vessels.
verses.15:16: And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all the days.
verses.15:17: And Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah, and he built Ramah so that there would be no one going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.
verses.15:18: And Asa took the silver and the gold that was found in the treasuries of the house of the king, and he gave them into the hands of his servants; and King Asa sent them to the son of Hader, son of Taberema, son of Hazin, king of Syria, who lived in Damascus, saying,
verses.15:19: "Make a covenant between me and my father and your father; look, I have sent you gifts, silver and gold; come, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, and he will go up from me."
verses.15:20: And the son of Hader listened to King Asa, and he sent the commanders of his own army against the cities of Israel; and they struck Ain, Dan, and Adelmath, and all Chezrath, as far as all the land of Naphtali.
verses.15:21: And it happened, when Baasha heard, that he stopped building Ramah and returned to Tirzah.
verses.15:22: And King Asa summoned all Judah to Ainakim, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timbers which Baasha had built, and with them King Asa built every hill of Benjamin and the watchtower.
verses.15:23: And the rest of the matters of Asa, and all his might which he performed, look, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Judah? Yet in the time of his old age he suffered pain in his feet.
verses.15:24: And Asa slept and was buried with his fathers in the city of David; and Jehoshaphat his son became king in his place.
verses.15:25: And Nebat son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned in Israel two years.
verses.15:26: And he did what was evil before the Lord, and he walked in the way of his father and in his sins by which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:27: And Baasha son of Ahijah besieged him at the house of Belaan; the son of Ahijah also wounded him at Gibbethon, which belonged to the foreigners; and Nebat and all Israel were besieging Gibbethon.
verses.15:28: And Baasha put him to death in the third year of King Asa son of Abiu, and he became king.
verses.15:29: And it happened, when he became king, that he struck the house of Jeroboam, and he did not leave behind any breath of Jeroboam until he destroyed him, according to the word of the Lord which He spoke by the hand of the servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
verses.15:30: because of the sins of Jeroboam, in that he caused Israel to sin, and in his provocation by which he provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger.
verses.15:31: And the rest of the matters of Nebat and all that he did, look, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.15:33: And in the third year of the king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah reigned over Israel in Tirzah twenty-four years.
verses.15:34: And he did what was evil before the Lord, and he walked in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins, in that he caused Israel to sin.
verses.16:1: And the word of the Lord came by the hand of Jehu son of Hanani to Baasha:
verses.16:2: "Because I lifted you up from the earth and appointed you leader over My people Israel, and you walked in the way of Jeroboam and caused My people Israel to sin, to provoke Me to anger with their worthless things,
verses.16:3: look, I am stirring up behind Baasha and behind his house, and I will make his house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
verses.16:4: The one of Baasha who dies in the city, the dogs will devour him, and the one of his who dies in the field, the birds of the sky will devour him."
verses.16:5: And the rest of the matters of Baasha and all that he did and his acts of might, look, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:6: And Baasha slept with his fathers, and he was buried in Tirzah; and Elah his son became king in his place in the twentieth year of King Asa.
verses.16:7: And by the hand of Jehu of Hanani the Lord spoke against Baasha and against his house regarding all the evil which he did before the Lord, to provoke Him to anger with the works of his hands, so as to be like the house of Jeroboam, and because he struck it.
verses.16:8: And Elah son of Baasha reigned over Israel two years in Tirzah.
verses.16:9: And Zimri, the commander of half of the cavalry, conspired against him, and he was in Tirzah drinking, drunk in the house of Osa, the steward in Tirzah.
verses.16:10: And Zimri went in and struck him and put him to death, and he became king in his place.
verses.16:11: And it happened, when he became king, when he sat on his throne, that he struck the whole house of Baasha,
verses.16:12: according to the word which the Lord spoke against the house of Baasha and to Jehu the prophet,
verses.16:13: because of all the sins of Baasha and of Elah his son, in that he caused Israel to sin, to provoke the Lord, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless things.
verses.16:14: And the rest of the matters of Elah which he did, look, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:15: And Zimri reigned seven years in Tirzah; and the camp of Israel was at Gibeon, which belonged to the foreigners.
verses.16:16: And the people in the camp heard them saying, "Zimri has conspired and struck the king." And in Israel they made Zimri, the leader of the army, king over Israel on that day in the camp.
verses.16:17: And Zimri went up, and all Israel with him, at Gibbethon, and they besieged Tirzah.
verses.16:18: And it happened, when Zimri saw that his city had already been captured, that they went into a cave of the house of the king, and the king burned the house of the king over him, and he died,
verses.16:19: for his sins which he committed, in doing what was evil before the Lord, walking in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins, in that he caused Israel to sin.
verses.16:20: And the rest of the matters of Zimri and his conspiracies which he formed, look, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:21: Then the people of Israel were divided: half of the people went after Tibni son of Ginath to make him king, and half of the people went after Zimri.
verses.16:22: And the people who were after Tibni son of Ginath were defeated; and Tibni died, and Joram his brother, at that time, and Zimri became king after Tibni.
verses.16:23: In the thirty-first year of King Asa, Zimri reigned over Israel twelve years; in Tirzah he reigned six years.
verses.16:24: And Zimri bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer, the owner of the hill, for two talents of silver, and he built the hill; and they called the name of the hill which they built, after the name of Shemer the owner of the hill, Samaria.
verses.16:25: And Zimri did what was evil before the Lord; he acted more wickedly than all who had been before him.
verses.16:26: And he walked in every way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins by which he caused Israel to sin, to provoke to anger with their worthless things.
verses.16:27: And the rest of the matters of Zimri and all that he did and his might, look, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:28: And Zimri slept with his fathers, and he was buried in Samaria; and Ahab his son became king in his place. And in the eleventh year of Zimri, Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king; he became king at thirty-five years of age in his reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Gabuza, daughter of Shilhi. And he walked in the way of Asa his father, and he did not turn aside from it, doing what was right before the Lord; yet they did not remove any of the high places; they sacrificed on the high places and burned incense. And what Jehoshaphat agreed upon, and all the might which he performed, and those against whom he waged war, look, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Judah? And the rest of the entanglements which they had set up in the days of Asa his father he removed from the land. And there was no king in Syria; a nasib was the king. He made a ship for Tarshish to go to Sophir, to go for the gold; and it did not go, because the ship was shattered at Ezion-geber. Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will send out your servants and my young servants in the ship." And Jehoshaphat was not willing. And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers in the city of David; and Joram his son became king in his place.
verses.16:29: In the second year of Jehoshaphat, Ahab son of Zimri became king; he reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.
verses.16:30: And Ahab did what was evil before the Lord; he acted more wickedly than all who were before him.
verses.16:31: And it was not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and he took as a wife Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and he went and served Baal and worshiped him.
verses.16:32: And he set up an altar to Baal in the house of his abominations which he had built in Samaria.
verses.16:33: And Ahab made a grove; and Ahab continued to commit provocations to provoke his own soul to anger, so as to be utterly destroyed; he did more evil than all the kings of Israel who had been before him.
verses.16:34: Hiel the Bethelite built Jericho; at the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and at the cost of Segub his youngest he set up its doors, according to the word of the Lord which He spoke by the hand of Joshua son of Nun.
verses.17:1: And Elijah the prophet, the Tishbite from Tishbe of Gilead, said to Ahab, "As the Lord, the God of powers, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I have stood, there will surely be no dew or rain during these years, except by the mouth of my word."
verses.17:2: And the word of the Lord came to Elijah:
verses.17:3: "Go from here toward the east, and hide yourself in the wadi of Cherith, which is facing the Jordan.
verses.17:4: And it will be that from the wadi you will drink water, and I will command the ravens to sustain you there."
verses.17:5: And Elijah did according to the word of the Lord, and he stayed in the wadi of Cherith facing the Jordan.
verses.17:6: And the ravens kept bringing him loaves of bread in the morning and meat in the evening, and he drank water from the wadi.
verses.17:7: And it happened after some days that the wadi dried up, because no rain had come upon the land.
verses.17:8: And the word of the Lord came to Elijah:
verses.17:9: "Rise and go to Zarephath of Sidon; look, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain you."
verses.17:10: And he rose and went to Zarephath, to the gate of the city; and look, there a widow woman was gathering sticks. And Elijah called out after her and said to her, "Please fetch a little water in a vessel, and I will drink."
verses.17:11: And she went to fetch it, and Elijah called out after her and said, "Please fetch for me a morsel of the bread that is in your hand."
verses.17:12: And the woman said, "As the Lord your God lives, I surely do not have a baked cake, except as much as a handful of flour in the jar and a little oil in the flask; and look, I am gathering two small sticks, and I will go in and prepare it for myself and for my children, and we will eat and die."
verses.17:13: And Elijah said to her, "Take courage, go in and do according to your word. Only make for me from it a small baked cake first, and you will bring it out to me, and for yourself and your children you will make some afterward,
verses.17:14: for thus says the Lord: 'The jar of flour will not fail and the flask of oil will not diminish until the day that the Lord gives rain upon the land.'"
verses.17:15: And the woman went and did so; and she and he and her children ate.
verses.17:16: And the jar of flour did not fail, and the flask of oil was not diminished, according to the word of the Lord that He spoke by the hand of Elijah.
verses.17:17: And it happened after these things that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became ill; and his illness was exceedingly severe, until no breath was left in him.
verses.17:18: And she said to Elijah, "What do I have to do with you, man of God? Have you come in to me to bring my unrighteousness to remembrance and to put my son to death?"
verses.17:19: And Elijah said to the woman, "Give me your son." And he took him from her bosom and carried him up into the upper room where he himself was staying, and laid him down on the bed.
verses.17:20: And Elijah cried out and said, "Alas, Lord, the witness of the widow with whom I dwell, You have done harm by putting her son to death."
verses.17:21: And he breathed upon the boy three times, and he called upon the Lord and said, "Lord my God, please let the soul of this boy return into him."
verses.17:22: And it happened so, and the boy cried out.
verses.17:23: And he brought him down from the upper room into the house and gave him to his mother; and Elijah said, "See, your son lives."
verses.17:24: And the woman said to Elijah, "Look, I know that you are a man of God, and the word of the Lord in your mouth is true."
verses.18:1: And it happened after many days that the word of the Lord came to Elijah in the third year, saying, "Go and appear to Ahab, and I will give rain on the face of the land."
verses.18:2: And Elijah went to appear to Ahab; and the famine was severe in Samaria.
verses.18:3: And Ahab called Obadiah the steward; and Obadiah greatly feared the Lord.
verses.18:4: And it happened, when Jezebel was striking down the prophets of the Lord, that Obadiah took a hundred men who were prophets and hid them by fifties in a cave, and sustained them with bread and water.
verses.18:5: And Ahab said to Obadiah, "Come, and let us pass through the land to the springs of water and to the wadis; perhaps we may find grass and preserve horses and mules, and they will not be destroyed from the tents."
verses.18:6: And they divided between themselves the way to pass through it; Ahab went by one way, and Obadiah went by another way alone.
verses.18:7: And Obadiah was on the way alone, and Elijah came to meet him alone; and Obadiah hurried and fell on his face and said, "Is it you yourself, my lord Elijah?"
verses.18:8: And Elijah said to him, "It is I. Go, tell your lord, 'Here is Elijah.'"
verses.18:9: And Obadiah said, "How have I sinned, that you are giving your servant into the hand of Ahab to put me to death?
verses.18:10: As the Lord your God lives, there is surely no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to search for you; and if they said, 'He is not here,' he burned down the kingdom and its regions, because he had not found you.
verses.18:11: And now you say, 'Go, report to your lord.'
verses.18:12: And it will happen that if I depart from you, the Spirit of the Lord will carry you away to a land that I do not know; and I will go in to report to Ahab, and he will kill me; yet your servant has feared the Lord from his youth.
verses.18:13: And was it not reported to you, my lord, what things I have done when Jezebel was killing the prophets of the Lord, that I hid a hundred men of the prophets of the Lord by fifties in a cave and fed them with loaves of bread and water?
verses.18:14: And now you say to me, 'Go, tell your lord, "Here is Elijah,"' and he will kill me."
verses.18:15: And Elijah said, "As the Lord of powers lives, before whom I have stood, today I will surely appear to him."
verses.18:16: And Obadiah went to meet Ahab and reported to him; and Ahab ran out and went to meet Elijah.
verses.18:17: And it happened, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said to Elijah, "Is it you yourself, the one who perverts Israel?"
verses.18:18: And Elijah said, "I am not perverting Israel, but rather you and the house of your father are, by forsaking the Lord your God; and you went after the Baals.
verses.18:19: And now send, gather to me all Israel to Mount Carmel, and the prophets of shame, four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the groves, four hundred, who eat at Jezebel's table."
verses.18:20: And Ahab sent to all Israel, and gathered all the prophets together to Mount Carmel.
verses.18:21: And Elijah drew near to all of them; and Elijah said to them, "How long will you limp on both knee-joints? If the Lord is God, go after Him; but if Baal, go after him." And the people did not answer a word.
verses.18:22: And Elijah said to the people, "I alone have been left as a prophet of the Lord, while the prophets of Baal are four hundred and fifty men, and the prophets of the grove are four hundred.
verses.18:23: Let them give us two oxen, and let them choose one for themselves, and cut it in pieces and lay it on the wood, and put no fire to it; and I will prepare the other ox, and I will certainly not put fire to it.
verses.18:24: And call out in the name of your gods, and I will call in the name of the Lord my God; and it will be that the god who answers by fire, that one is God." And all the people answered and said, "The word that you have spoken is good."
verses.18:25: And Elijah said to the prophets of shame, "Choose for yourselves the one young bull and prepare it first, because you are many, and call in the name of your god, and put no fire to it."
verses.18:26: And they took the young bull and prepared it, and they kept calling in the name of Baal from morning until noon, and said, "Answer us, Baal, answer us." And there was no voice and there was no response; and they kept running about on the altar that they had made.
verses.18:27: And it became noon, and Elijah the Tishbite mocked them and said, "Call out with a loud voice, because he is a god; because he is occupied in conversation, and at the same time perhaps he is transacting business, or perhaps he is asleep and will wake up."
verses.18:28: And they kept calling out with a loud voice, and they kept cutting themselves with a sword and with lances until blood poured out upon them,
verses.18:29: and they prophesied until the afternoon passed. And it happened, around the time for the sacrifice to be offered up, that Elijah spoke to the prophets of the abominations, saying, "Step aside from now on, and I will prepare my burnt offering." And they stepped aside and departed.
verses.18:30: And Elijah said to the people, "Draw near to me." And all the people drew near to him.
verses.18:31: And Elijah took twelve stones according to the number of the tribes of Israel, as the Lord spoke to him, saying, "Israel will be your name."
verses.18:32: And he built the stones in the name of the Lord, and he healed the altar that had been torn down, and he made a sea holding two measures of seed around the altar.
verses.18:33: And he stacked the split wood on the altar that he had made, and he cut the burnt offering in pieces and placed the split wood on it, and stacked it on the altar.
verses.18:34: And he said, "Fetch for me four jars of water, and pour it on the burnt offering and on the split wood." And they did so. And he said, "Do it a second time." And they did it a second time. And he said, "Do it a third time." And they did it a third time.
verses.18:35: And the water flowed around the altar, and they filled the sea with water.
verses.18:36: And Elijah cried out to heaven and said, "Lord, God of Abraham and Isaac and Israel, answer me, Lord, answer me today by fire, and let all this people know that You are the Lord, the God of Israel, and I am Your servant, and because of You I have done these works.
verses.18:37: Answer me, Lord, answer me, and let this people know that You are the Lord God, and that You have turned the heart of this people back."
verses.18:38: And fire fell from the Lord out of heaven, and consumed the burnt offerings and the split wood and the water that was in the sea, and the fire licked up the stones and the dust.
verses.18:39: And all the people fell on their faces and said, "Truly the Lord is God; He is God."
verses.18:40: And Elijah said to the people, "Seize the prophets of Baal; let not one of them escape." And they seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the wadi of Kishon and slaughtered them there.
verses.18:41: And Elijah said to Ahab, "Go up and eat and drink, for there is a sound of the feet of the rain."
verses.18:42: And Ahab went up to eat and drink; and Elijah went up onto Carmel, and bowed down to the ground and put his face between his knees,
verses.18:43: and said to his young attendant, "Go up and look toward the sea." And the young attendant looked and said, "There is nothing." And Elijah said, "And you, go back seven times, and return seven times."
verses.18:44: And the young attendant returned seven times; and it happened on the seventh time, and look, a small cloud like the footprint of a man, bringing up water. And he said, "Go up and say to Ahab, 'Hitch up your chariot and go down, so that the rain does not overtake you.'"
verses.18:45: And it happened in a little while that the sky grew dark with clouds and wind, and the rain became heavy; and Ahab wept and went to Israel.
verses.18:46: And the hand of the Lord was upon Elijah; and he bound up his waist, and ran ahead of Ahab to Israel.
verses.19:1: And Ahab reported to Jezebel his wife all that Elijah had done, and how he had killed the prophets with the sword.
verses.19:2: And Jezebel sent to Elijah and said, "If you are Elijah and I am Jezebel, may God do thus to me and add thus, that at this hour tomorrow I will make your life like the life of one of them."
verses.19:3: And Elijah was afraid, and he arose and departed for his own life, and he came to Beersheba, the land of Judah, and left his young servant there.
verses.19:4: And he himself went in the wilderness a day's journey, and came and sat down beneath a broom bush. And he asked for his life to die, and said, "Let it be enough now; please take my life from me, Lord, for I am no better than my fathers."
verses.19:5: And he lay down and fell asleep there under a plant; and look, someone touched him and said to him, "Arise and eat."
verses.19:6: And Elijah looked, and look, at his head was a spelt cake baked in ashes and a flask of water. And he arose and ate and drank, and turning back, he lay down.
verses.19:7: And the angel of the Lord returned a second time, and touched him and said to him, "Arise, eat, for the journey is too great for you."
verses.19:8: And he arose and ate and drank, and he went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights as far as Mount Horeb.
verses.19:9: And he entered there into the cave and lodged there; and look, the word of the Lord came to him and said, "Why are you here, Elijah?"
verses.19:10: And Elijah said, "With zeal I have been zealous for the Lord Almighty, because the sons of Israel have forsaken You; they have demolished Your altars and killed Your prophets with the sword, and I am left all alone, and they seek my life, to take it."
verses.19:11: And He said, "You shall go out tomorrow and stand before the Lord on the mountain; look, the Lord will pass by." And there was a great, mighty wind breaking up mountains and shattering rocks before the Lord, in the wind of the Lord; and after the wind, an earthquake; the Lord was not in the earthquake;
verses.19:12: and after the earthquake, a fire; the Lord was not in the fire; and after the fire, the sound of a light breeze.
verses.19:13: And it happened, when Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his sheepskin cloak, and he went out and stood beneath the cave; and look, a voice came to him and said, "Why are you here, Elijah?"
verses.19:14: And Elijah said, "With zeal I have been zealous for the Lord Almighty, because the sons of Israel have forsaken You; they have overthrown Your covenant and Your altars and killed Your prophets with the sword, and I am left all alone, and they seek my life, to take it."
verses.19:15: And the Lord said to him, "Go, return on your way, and you shall come to the way of the wilderness of Damascus; and you shall come and anoint Hazael as king of Syria;
verses.19:16: and you shall anoint the son of Jehu, son of Nimshi, as king over Israel; and you shall anoint Elisha son of Shaphat, from Abel-meholah, as prophet in your place.
verses.19:17: And it will be that the one who escapes from the sword of Hazael, Jehu will put to death, and the one who escapes from the sword of Jehu, Elisha will put to death.
verses.19:18: And you will leave in Israel seven thousand men, all the knees that have not bent the knee to Baal, and every mouth that has not worshiped him."
verses.19:19: And he departed from there and found Elisha son of Shaphat, and he was plowing with oxen; twelve yokes were before him, and he was among the twelve. He came up to him and threw his sheepskin cloak upon him.
verses.19:20: And Elisha left the oxen and ran after Elijah and said, "Let me kiss my father, and I will follow after you." And Elijah said, "Return, for I have done it to you."
verses.19:21: And he returned from behind him, and took the yokes of oxen and slaughtered and boiled them with the equipment of the oxen, and gave it to the people, and they ate. And he arose and went after Elijah, and served him.
verses.20:1: And there was a certain vineyard belonging to Naboth the Israelite beside the threshing floor of Ahab king of Samaria.
verses.20:2: And Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, "Give me your vineyard, and it shall be a vegetable garden for me, because this one is nearer to my house, and I will give you another vineyard better than it; or if it is pleasing in your sight, I will give you silver in exchange for this vineyard of yours, and it shall be a vegetable garden for me."
verses.20:3: And Naboth said to Ahab, "May it never happen to me from my God to give the inheritance of my fathers to you."
verses.20:4: And the spirit of Ahab became troubled, and he lay down on his bed and covered his face, and he did not eat bread.
verses.20:5: And Jezebel his wife came in to him and spoke to him, "Why is your spirit troubled, and why are you not eating bread?"
verses.20:6: And he said to her, "Because I spoke to Naboth the Israelite, saying, 'Give me your vineyard for silver; or if you wish, I will give you another vineyard in its place.' And he said, 'I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers.'"
verses.20:7: And Jezebel his wife said to him, "Is this how you now act the king over Israel? Arise, eat bread, and come to yourself; I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Israelite."
verses.20:8: And she wrote a letter in the name of Ahab and sealed it with his seal, and sent the letter to the elders and the free men who lived with Naboth.
verses.20:9: And it was written in the letters, saying, "Fast a fast, and seat Naboth at the head of the people;
verses.20:10: and station two men, sons of lawless men."
verses.20:11: And the men of his city, the elders and the free men who lived in his city, did just as Jezebel had sent to them, and as it was written in the letters that she had sent to them.
verses.20:12: And they called a fast, and seated Naboth at the head of the people.
verses.20:13: And they sat down opposite him and testified against him, saying, "You have blessed God and the king." And they led him outside the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.
verses.20:14: And they sent to Jezebel, saying, "Naboth has been stoned and is dead."
verses.20:15: And it happened, when Jezebel heard it, she said to Ahab, "Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Israelite, who did not give it to you for silver; for Naboth is not alive, because he is dead."
verses.20:16: And it happened, when Ahab heard that Naboth the Israelite was dead, he tore his garments and put on sackcloth. And it happened after these things, Ahab arose and went down to the vineyard of Naboth the Israelite to take possession of it.
verses.20:17: And the Lord spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
verses.20:18: "Arise and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria; for he is in the vineyard of Naboth, because he has gone down there to take possession of it.
verses.20:19: And you shall speak to him, saying, 'Thus says the Lord: Since you have murdered and taken possession, therefore thus says the Lord: In every place where the swine and the dogs licked up the blood of Naboth, there the dogs will lick up your blood, and the prostitutes will wash themselves in your blood.'"
verses.20:20: And Ahab said to Elijah, "Have you found me, my enemy?" And he said, "I have found you, because you have been sold in vain to do what is evil before the Lord, to provoke Him to anger.
verses.20:21: Look, I am bringing calamities upon you, and I will burn up after you, and I will utterly destroy from Ahab anyone who urinates against a wall, both confined and forsaken in Israel.
verses.20:22: And I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the provocations with which you have provoked anger and have caused Israel to sin.
verses.20:23: And concerning Jezebel the Lord has spoken, saying, 'The dogs will devour her in the outer wall of Israel.'
verses.20:24: The one of Ahab who dies in the city, the dogs will eat, and the one of his who dies in the field, the birds of the sky will eat."
verses.20:25: Yet in vain was Ahab, since he was sold to do what is evil before the Lord, as Jezebel his wife turned him aside;
verses.20:26: and he became exceedingly abominable in going after the abominations, according to all that the Amorite had done, whom the Lord had utterly destroyed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.20:27: And because of the word, when Ahab was stricken with remorse before the Lord, he went about weeping, and tore his tunic, and fastened sackcloth upon his body, and fasted; and he put on sackcloth on the day that he struck down Naboth the Israelite, and went on.
verses.20:28: And the word of the Lord came by the hand of His servant Elijah concerning Ahab, and the Lord said,
verses.20:29: "Have you seen how Ahab has been stricken with remorse before Me? I will not bring the calamity in his days; and in the days of his son I will bring the calamity."
verses.21:1: And Son of Hader gathered all his army together and went up and besieged Samaria, and thirty-two kings were with him, and every horse and chariot; and they went up and besieged Samaria, and fought against it.
verses.21:2: And he sent to Ahab, king of Israel, into the city and said to him, "Thus says Son of Hader:
verses.21:3: Your silver and your gold are mine, and your wives and your children are mine."
verses.21:4: And the king of Israel answered and said, "Just as you have spoken, lord king, I am yours, and all that is mine."
verses.21:5: And the messengers returned and said, "Thus says Son of Hader: I sent back, saying, 'Your silver and your gold and your wives you shall give to me,'
verses.21:6: for at this hour tomorrow I will send my servants to you, and they will search your house and the houses of your servants; and it will be that whatever desirable things of their eyes they lay their hands on, they will take."
verses.21:7: And the king of Israel called all the elders and said, "Know now and see that this man is seeking evil, for he has sent to me concerning my wives and concerning my sons and concerning my daughters; my silver and my gold I did not withhold from him."
verses.21:8: And the elders and all the people said to him, "Do not listen, and do not consent."
verses.21:9: And he said to the messengers of Son of Hader, "Say to your lord, 'All that you sent to your servant at first I will do, but this thing I will not be able to do.'" And the men departed and brought back word to him.
verses.21:10: And Son of Hader sent to him, saying, "So may God do to me, and so may He add, if the dust of Samaria will suffice for the foxes, for all the people, my foot soldiers."
verses.21:11: And the king of Israel answered and said, "Let it be enough; do not let the hunchbacked man boast like the upright man."
verses.21:12: And it came about, when he answered him this word, that he was drinking, he and all the kings with him, in tents; and he said to his servants, "Build a palisade." And they set up a palisade against the city.
verses.21:13: And look, one prophet approached the king of Israel and said, "Thus says the Lord: Have you seen this great multitude? Look, I am giving it today into your hands, and you will know that I am the Lord."
verses.21:14: And Ahab said, "By whom?" And he said, "Thus says the Lord: By the young men of the rulers of the districts." And Ahab said, "Who will begin the battle?" And he said, "You."
verses.21:15: And Ahab mustered the rulers, the young men of the districts, and they were two hundred and thirty; and after these things he mustered the people, every son of might, sixty.
verses.21:16: And he went out at noon; and Son of Hader was drinking, drunk, in Succoth, he and the kings, thirty-two, allied kings with him.
verses.21:17: And the rulers, the young men of the districts, went out first; and they sent and reported to the king of Syria, saying, "Men have come out from Samaria."
verses.21:18: "Tell them, for peace—for they are not coming out—to seize them alive; and for war, to seize them alive;
verses.21:19: and let not the ruling young men, ruling the districts, come out from the city, and the army behind them."
verses.21:20: Each struck the one beside him, and each struck a second time the one beside him, and Syria fled; and Israel pursued them, and Son of Hader, king of Syria, escaped on a horseman's horse.
verses.21:21: And the king of Israel went out and took all the horses and the chariots, and struck a great blow against Syria.
verses.21:22: And the prophet approached the king of Israel and said, "Strengthen yourself, and know and see what you will do, for at the return of the year Son of Hader, king of Syria, is coming up against you."
verses.21:23: And the servants of the king of Syria said, "A god of mountains is the God of Israel, and not a god of a valley; therefore He was stronger than us; but if we fight them on level ground, surely we will be stronger than them.
verses.21:24: And do this thing: remove the kings, each to their place, and put satraps in their place,
verses.21:25: and we will replace for you an army like the army that fell, and horse like the horse, and chariots like the chariots, and we will fight against them on level ground, and we will be stronger than them." And he listened to his voice, and did so.
verses.21:26: And it came about at the return of the year that Son of Hader mustered Syria, and went up to Aphek for war against Israel.
verses.21:27: And the sons of Israel were mustered, and came to meet them, and Israel encamped opposite them like two flocks of goats, and Syria filled the land.
verses.21:28: And the man of God approached and said to the king of Israel, "Thus says the Lord: Because Syria has said, 'A god of mountains is the Lord God of Israel, and not a god of valleys is He,' I will give this great army into your hand, and you will know that I am the Lord;
verses.21:29: and these will encamp opposite those for seven days." And it came about on the seventh day that the battle drew near, and Israel struck Syria, one hundred thousand foot soldiers in one day.
verses.21:30: And those who remained fled to Aphek, into the city, and the wall fell on twenty-seven thousand of the men who remained; and Son of Hader fled and went into the house of the bedroom, into the inner room.
verses.21:31: And he said to his servants, "I know that the kings of Israel are kings of mercy; let us now put sackcloth on our waists and ropes on our heads, and let us still go out to the king of Israel, if perhaps he will keep our souls alive."
verses.21:32: And they tied sackcloth around their waists and put ropes on their heads, and said to the king of Israel, "Your servant Son of Hader says, 'Please let our soul live.'" And he said, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."
verses.21:33: And the men took it as an omen and made a truce, and picked up the word from his mouth and said, "Your brother is Son of Hader." And he said, "Go in and get him." And Son of Hader came out to him, and they brought him up to him onto the chariot.
verses.21:34: And he said to him, "The cities that my father took from your father I will return to you, and you will set up streets for yourself in Damascus, just as my father set up in Samaria." "And I will send you away with a covenant." And he made a covenant with him, and sent him away.
verses.21:35: And one man from the sons of the prophets said to his neighbor by the word of the Lord, "Please strike me." And the man was not willing to strike him.
verses.21:36: And he said to him, "Because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord, look, you are running away from me, and a lion will strike you." And he departed from him, and a lion found him and struck him.
verses.21:37: And he found another man and said, "Please strike me." And the man struck him; striking him, he bruised him.
verses.21:38: And the prophet went and stood for the king of Israel on the road, and bound his eyes with a bandage.
verses.21:39: And it came about, as the king was passing by, that this man cried out to the king and said, "Your servant went out to the campaign of war, and look, a man brought out a man to me and said to me, 'Guard this man; and if he indeed escapes, then your life shall be in place of his life, or you shall weigh out a talent of silver.'
verses.21:40: And it happened, your servant looked around here and there, and this man was not there." And the king of Israel said to him, "Look, you have also murdered the ambushes with me."
verses.21:41: And he hurried and removed the bandage from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him, that he was one of the prophets.
verses.21:42: And he said to him, "Thus says the Lord: Because you yourself have let a destructive man out of your hand, your life shall be in place of his life, and your people in place of his people."
verses.21:43: And the king of Israel departed, confounded and disheartened, and came to Samaria.
verses.22:1: And he remained three years, and there was no war between Syria and Israel.
verses.22:2: And it happened in the third year that Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to the king of Israel.
verses.22:3: And the king of Israel said to his servants, "Do you know that Ramoth-gilead belongs to us, and we are keeping silent about taking it from the hand of the king of Syria?"
verses.22:4: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Will you go up with us to Ramoth-gilead to battle?"
verses.22:5: And Jehoshaphat said, "As I am, so also are you; as my people are, so are your people; as my horses are, so are your horses." And Jehoshaphat king of Judah said to the king of Israel, "Please inquire of the Lord today."
verses.22:6: And the king of Israel gathered together all the prophets, about four hundred men, and the king said to them, "Should I go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or hold back?" And they said, "Go up, and the Lord will surely give it into the hands of the king."
verses.22:7: And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Is there not a prophet of the Lord here, that we may inquire of the Lord through him?"
verses.22:8: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is one man through whom to inquire of the Lord, and I hate him, because he does not speak good concerning me, but only evil, Micaiah son of Jemias." And Jehoshaphat king of Judah said, "Let the king not say so."
verses.22:9: And the king of Israel called one eunuch and said, "Quickly, Micaiah son of Jemias!"
verses.22:10: And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting, each man on his throne, armed, in the gates of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
verses.22:11: And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made iron horns for himself and said, "Thus says the Lord, 'With these you will gore Syria until it is brought to an end.'"
verses.22:12: And all the prophets were prophesying in this way, saying, "Go up to Ramoth-gilead, and it will prosper; and the Lord will give into your hands even the king of Syria."
verses.22:13: And the messenger who went to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, "Look now, all the prophets are speaking with their mouth for good concerning the king; now you also be one in your words, according to the words of one of these, and speak good."
verses.22:14: And Micaiah said, "As the Lord lives, whatever the Lord says to me, these things I will speak."
verses.22:15: And he came to the king, and the king said to him, "Micaiah, should I go up to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or hold back?" And he said, "Go up, and the Lord will prosper it into the hand of the king."
verses.22:16: And the king said to him, "Five times I put you under oath that you speak truth to me in the name of the Lord."
verses.22:17: And he said, "Not so. I have seen all Israel scattered on the mountains like a flock that has no shepherd; and the Lord said, 'Is the Lord not God to these? Let each one return to his house in peace.'"
verses.22:18: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Did I not say to you, 'This man does not prophesy good for me, but only evil'?"
verses.22:19: And Micaiah said, "Not so. Not I; hear the word of the Lord; not so, I saw the God of Israel sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven was standing around Him on His right and on His left.
verses.22:20: And the Lord said, 'Who will deceive Ahab king of Israel, so that he will go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' And one spoke in this way, and another in that way.
verses.22:21: And a spirit came out and stood before the Lord and said, 'I will deceive him.'
verses.22:22: And the Lord said to him, 'By what means?' And he said, 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' And He said, 'You will deceive him, and indeed you will prevail; go out and do so.'
verses.22:23: And now, look, the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and the Lord has spoken evil against you."
verses.22:24: And Zedekiah son of Canaan approached and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said, "What kind of spirit of the Lord is it that spoke in you?"
verses.22:25: And Micaiah said, "Look, you will see on that day when you enter a chamber of the hidden chamber."
verses.22:26: And the king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and return him to Semer the king of the city; and to Joash the son of the king
verses.22:27: say to put this man in prison, and that he eat bread of affliction and water of affliction until I return in peace."
verses.22:28: And Micaiah said, "If you indeed return in peace, the Lord has not spoken in me."
verses.22:29: And the king of Israel went up, and Jehoshaphat king of Judah with him, to Ramoth-gilead.
verses.22:30: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "I will disguise myself and enter into the battle, and you put on my apparel." And the king of Israel disguised himself and entered into the battle.
verses.22:31: And the king of Syria commanded the thirty-two commanders of his chariots, saying, "Do not fight small or great, except the king of Israel alone."
verses.22:32: And it happened, when the commanders of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat king of Judah, that they said, "It appears this is the king of Israel." And they surrounded him to fight, and Jehoshaphat cried out.
verses.22:33: And it happened, when the commanders of the chariots saw that this was not the king of Israel, that they turned back from him.
verses.22:34: And one man drew the bow with good aim and struck the king of Israel between the lung and the breastplate; and he said to his charioteer, "Turn your hands around and bring me out of the battle, because I have been wounded."
verses.22:35: And the battle turned on that day; and the king was standing on the chariot facing Syria from morning until evening, and blood was pouring out from the wound into the hollow of the chariot; and he died in the evening, and the blood of the defeat was flowing out as far as the hollow of the chariot.
verses.22:36: And the army herald stood as the sun was setting, saying, "Each one to his own city and to his own land,
verses.22:37: because the king is dead." And they came to Samaria, and they buried the king in Samaria.
verses.22:38: And they washed off the blood at the spring of Samaria, and the pigs and the dogs licked up the blood, and the prostitutes washed themselves in the blood, according to the word of the Lord which He spoke.
verses.22:39: And the rest of the matters of Ahab, and all that he did, and an ivory house which he built, and all the cities which he made, look, these are written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel.
verses.22:40: And Ahab slept with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
verses.22:41: And Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king over Judah; in the fourth year of Ahab he became king.
verses.22:42: Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shimei.
verses.22:43: And he walked in all the way of Asa his father; he did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the Lord.
verses.22:44: Yet he did not remove the high places; the people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.
verses.22:45: And Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
verses.22:46: And the rest of the matters of Jehoshaphat, and his mighty deeds, all that he did, look, are these not written in the book of the records of Jehoshaphat?
verses.22:51: And he slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David his father; and Joram his son reigned in his place.
verses.22:52: And Ahaziah son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah; and he reigned in Israel two years.
verses.22:53: And he did what was evil before the Lord, and he walked in the way of his father Ahab and in the way of Jezebel his mother and in the sins of the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat who caused Israel to sin.
verses.22:54: And he served the Baals and worshiped them, and provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger according to all the things that had happened before him. And Moab rebelled against Israel after Ahab died.

notes.1:8: Greek reads Resei (corresponding to Hebrew Rei) and 'mighty sons of David' (where the Hebrew text and some Greek witnesses read 'the mighty men who belonged to David').
notes.1:9: Greek reads 'by Aithe of Zoheleth, which was next to Rogel' (where the Hebrew and some Greek witnesses read 'by the stone of Zoheleth, which is beside En-rogel'), and 'the prominent men of Judah' rather than 'all the men of Judah'.
notes.1:40: Greek reads 'dancing in dances' (reflecting the Hebrew root for dancing), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads 'playing on flutes'.
notes.1:48: Greek explicitly includes 'from my seed' before 'sitting on my throne,' a phrase not present in the Masoretic Hebrew text.
notes.1:52: Greek uses a Hebraistic oath conditional ('if') to express an emphatic negative ('not one of his hairs will fall'), and reads passive 'he will be put to death' where the Hebrew has 'he shall die'.
notes.2:6: The Greek text reads "and you shall bring down" (καὶ σὺ κατάξεις) without the negation found in the Hebrew ("do not let ... go down"), likely reflecting an early uncial confusion between ΟΥ ("not") and ΣΥ ("you").
notes.2:34: The Greek text names "Jehoiada" (Ἰωδᾶε) as Joab's executioner, omitting "Benaiah son of" before his father's name.
notes.2:35: The Septuagint inserts an extensive summary of Solomon's wisdom, building works, and David's charge concerning Shimei not placed here in the Hebrew text. It preserves distinct Greek forms and details, including "Magao" (corresponding to Megiddo), "Upper Beth-horon" (Hebrew "Lower"), and Shimei's origin "from Hebron" rather than Bahurim (cf. 2:8).
notes.2:39: The Greek text names Achish's father "Amesa" (Ἀμησά) rather than Maacah as in the Hebrew text.
notes.2:46: The Septuagint appends a second summary of Solomon's reign, provisions, and officials not placed here in the Hebrew text. Distinct Septuagint proper names are preserved—"Thermai" (Tamar/Tadmor), "Raphei" (Tiphsah), and the official names "Orniou," "Suba," "Basa son of Achithalam," "Abi son of Joab," "Achire son of Edrai," and "Kachour"—along with "the foreigners" (ἀλλοφύλων), the Septuagint's regular term for the Philistines.
notes.3:2: The Greek text omits verse 1 and the opening clause of verse 2 (found in the Hebrew), beginning abruptly with the participle "burning incense."
notes.3:15: The Greek adds that Solomon stood "before the altar that was before the ark of the covenant of the Lord in Zion" and made "a great banquet for himself," expanding on the shorter Hebrew text.
notes.3:17: "Pardon me, lord" translates the Septuagint idiom "in me, lord" (en emoi, kyrie; also in v. 26), a literal rendering of the Hebrew entreaty particle bi; the plural "we gave birth" also differs from the Hebrew singular.
notes.3:26: "Her womb was stirred" renders the Greek literally (he metra autes), reflecting the Hebrew idiom for deep maternal compassion.
notes.3:27: The Greek clarifies the king's verdict by explicitly adding "to the one who said" before quoting the first woman's plea, whereas the Hebrew simply reads "Give her the living child."
notes.4:3: In verses 2-6, the Greek cabinet list preserves several names and entries differing from the Hebrew: Azari (Heb. Azariah), Eliaph (Heb. Elihoreph), Saba (Heb. Shisha), Ornia (Heb. Azariah), Ahi (Heb. Ahishar), Ephra (Heb. Abda), plus Eliak and Eliab son of Saph (absent from the Hebrew), while omitting Benaiah in verse 4.
notes.4:8: In verses 8-9, the Greek preserves several names differing from the Hebrew: Baior (Heb. Ben-hur), Rechas (Heb. Deker), Machemas (Heb. Makaz), Bethalami (Heb. Shaalbim), and Bethlaman (Heb. Beth-hanan), and concludes districts with the tally "one."
notes.4:10: In verses 10-11, the Greek transliterates corrupted phrases as proper names: Bernemalousamencha and Respharachein (Heb. "in Arubboth; to him belonged Socoh and all the land of Hepher"), and "throughout Dan and throughout Phathei, husband of Tablethei" (Heb. "Ben-abinadab, all Naphath-dor; Taphath").
notes.4:12: In verses 12-16, the Greek preserves distinct forms including Baccha son of Ahimach, Polamach, "the house of Dan," Sesathan, Esrae, Baisaphut, and Maeber Lukam (v. 12); Eretabam (v. 13, Heb. Argob); Ahinaab son of Achel (v. 14, Heb. Ahinadab son of Iddo); and Maala (v. 16, Heb. Asher and Bealoth).
notes.4:18: Verses 17-19 follow the Septuagint order (placing Benjamin and Gad before Issachar) and preserve distinct readings: "son of Ela" without Shimei (v. 17), "son of Adai" in "the land of Gad" of Sihon king of "Heshbon" and "one naseph"—an untranslated transliteration of Hebrew netsib ("officer")—in Judah (v. 18), and Phuasud (v. 19, Heb. Paruah).
notes.5:9: Verses 5:5-8 of the standard numbering are absent at this point in the Septuagint (their material appears elsewhere in Greek 1 Kings, especially chapter 2 and chapter 4); nothing has been omitted from the Greek text.
notes.5:11: The Greek preserves distinct forms of these names (Gaithan the Zareite, Ainan, Chalkad, and Darala) and reads singular "son of Mal," corresponding to Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, sons of Mahol, in the Hebrew text.
notes.5:14: The Greek places the account of Pharaoh's daughter and Gezer here rather than in chapters 3 and 9, names the Canaanite city Mergab, and has no separate verb for killing the Canaanite.
notes.5:15: The Greek reads "to anoint Solomon," whereas the Hebrew text reads "because he heard that they had anointed him king."
notes.5:20: The Greek lacks "wages" before "your service" and reads the adverb idios ("on our own"), which may reflect an ancient orthographic variant of eidos ("one who knows how").
notes.5:25: "Macheir" is an untranslated Greek transliteration corresponding to Hebrew "food" or "provisions," and the Greek specifies twenty thousand baths of oil rather than twenty kors.
notes.6:1: The Greek dates the work to the 440th year after the departure from Egypt (rather than the 480th), reads "sons" where the Hebrew has "builders," and gives the month names as Niso and Baad (corresponding to Ziv and Bul).
notes.6:3: "Ailam" is a Greek transliteration of the Hebrew architectural term ulam, denoting the porch or vestibule of the temple.
notes.6:5: "Dabir" is a Greek transliteration of the Hebrew architectural term debir, denoting the inner sanctuary of the temple.
notes.6:15: Verses 6:11-14 of the Hebrew numbering (the Lord's conditional promise to Solomon) are absent from the Septuagint; nothing has been omitted from the Greek text.
notes.6:19: Verse 6:18 of the standard numbering is absent from the Septuagint at this point; nothing has been omitted from the Greek text.
notes.6:21: "Enclosed gold" literally translates Greek synkekleismeno, reflecting the Hebrew idiom for refined, choice gold.
notes.6:26: The Greek omits the numeral "ten" before "by the cubit" here, and similarly compresses the wing measurements in verse 24.
notes.6:34: Verses 6:32-33 of the standard numbering are absent from the Septuagint here; nothing has been omitted from the Greek text.
notes.6:36: The closing sentence ("And he built a curtain of the court of the ailam...") is a distinctive Septuagint reading with no counterpart in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.7:3: The Greek reads "the ailam" (transliterating Hebrew ulam, the porch) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text mentions casting the two bronze pillars, and gives the pillar's circumference as fourteen cubits rather than twelve.
notes.7:7: The Greek preserves the distinct pillar names Jachum (Iachoum) and Balaz (Balaz), corresponding to Jachin and Boaz in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.7:10: The Greek uniquely reads "from its wall to its brim" (compared to "from brim to brim" in Hebrew) and gives the measurement as thirty-three cubits "gathered together" rather than a thirty-cubit measuring line.
notes.7:33: Seira is the Septuagint's distinct proper name for the site called Zarethan in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.7:38: In the Greek order of 3 Kingdoms, Solomon's palace (7:38-50) follows Hiram's bronze furnishings (7:1-37), reversing the sequence of the Hebrew Masoretic Text (1 Kings 7:1-12 and 7:13-51); in 7:48-49, the Greek also specifies "unhewn stones" (apeleketon) where the Hebrew has hewn stone.
notes.8:2: Greek reads "Athamein" (a metathesized form of the Hebrew month name "Ethanim") and omits the longer assembly and festival notice found in the Masoretic Text of vv. 1-2, while v. 1 opens with the twenty-year building completion notice.
notes.8:6: The term rendered "inner sanctuary" here and in v. 8 transliterates the Hebrew architectural term directly into Greek as "dabir."
notes.8:8: Where the Masoretic Text refers to the ark's poles, the Greek text reads "its holy things" (v. 7) and "the consecrated things" (v. 8), and omits "and they are there to this day."
notes.8:11: Verses 12-13 are absent at this point in the Greek Septuagint; Solomon's poetic pronouncement on the temple appears instead after v. 53.
notes.8:28: Greek "delight" (terpsis) reflects the joyful sense of Hebrew rinnah ("ringing cry" or "shout of joy"), and Greek also includes "to You" alongside "before You."
notes.8:46: Greek reads "bring them" (epaxeis autous) where the Masoretic Text reads "be angry with them."
notes.8:53: The Septuagint places Solomon's poetic pronouncement here (corresponding to MT vv. 12-13), reading "made known the sun," "dwell in thick darkness" (lit. "out of thick darkness"), "Build my house... to dwell in newness," and citing "the book of the song" (a transposed reading of Hebrew "Book of Jashar").
notes.8:59: Greek shifts to second person ("Your servant Israel") and renders the closing idiom literally as "the matter of a day in the day of the year," expressing each day's need throughout the year.
notes.8:63: The Greek text lists only twenty-two thousand oxen, omitting the one hundred twenty thousand sheep found in the Masoretic Text.
notes.8:65: The Greek text adds "in the house which he built, eating and drinking and rejoicing before the Lord our God" and specifies seven days (omitting the additional seven days in MT); in v. 66 Greek also reads "he blessed them" rather than "they blessed the king."
notes.8:66: Greek agathe he kardia literally reads "the heart [was] good" (echoing "the good things," tois agathois), an idiom meaning "glad" or "cheerful" (compare 2 Chr 7:10).
notes.9:2: The Greek text reads 'Gabaoth,' a variant form of Gibeon.
notes.9:9: The closing sentence about Pharaoh's daughter appears here in the Septuagint rather than at 9:24 as in the Hebrew text, and the Greek makes Solomon the subject bringing her up to his own house.
notes.9:13: The Greek names the region Horion ('Border'), whereas the Hebrew text reads 'Cabul.' Verses 9:15-25 of the Hebrew text are absent from chapter 9 in the Septuagint, with most of that material appearing in 10:22.
notes.9:26: The Greek phrase 'hyper hou' ('for himself' or 'on this account') is textually difficult; the Greek also reads the variant spelling 'Emaeseion-gaber' for Ezion-geber and 'the farthest sea' where the Hebrew text reads the Sea of Reeds (Red Sea).
notes.9:28: The Greek reads the distinct place name 'Sophera' (corresponding to Hebrew 'Ophir'; compare 'Suphir' in 10:11) and gives the weight as 120 talents of gold rather than 420 talents as in the Hebrew text.
notes.10:11: The Greek reads the distinct place name 'Suphir' (corresponding to Hebrew 'Ophir') and 'hewn timbers' where the Hebrew text specifies almug wood.
notes.10:16: The Greek records three hundred spears with three hundred gold pieces on each, differing from the Hebrew text's two hundred large shields of six hundred shekels each.
notes.10:19: The Greek reads 'busts of calves' (protomai moschon) at the back of the throne, whereas the Hebrew text describes a rounded top.
notes.10:22: The Greek lists a cargo of carved and hewn stones and incorporates the building and forced-labor account corresponding to Hebrew 9:15-22, with distinct place names ('Asshur,' 'Midian,' 'Upper Beth-horon,' and 'Jethermath' for Hebrew Hazor, Megiddo, Lower Beth-horon, and Baalath/Tamar). The clause 'so that all the people indicated by...' reflects a distinct Greek rendering of the Hebrew text and an early Greek textual variant for 'left over.'
notes.10:28: The Greek reads the distinct place name 'Tekoa' (Thekoue), corresponding to 'Kue' (or 'droves') in the Hebrew text, and speaks of 'horsemen' rather than horses; in 10:29 the Greek likewise gives lower prices (100 and 50 pieces of silver) and reads 'by sea' instead of 'by their hand.'
notes.11:5: Greek renders Hebrew Molech/Milcom as "their king" (also in 11:33), and rearranges the material of MT 11:1-8 (omitting v. 3, whose numbers appear in v. 1).
notes.11:13: "Tribe" translates Greek skeptron (lit., "scepter"), an LXX idiom for Hebrew shevet ("staff, scepter, tribe") used throughout chs. 11-12; contrast the LXX reading "two tribes" in 11:32 and 11:36 (MT "one tribe").
notes.11:14: Greek merges MT 11:14 and 11:23-25a here, transliterates "adversary" as satan, and preserves the distinct names Hader (MT Hadad), Hesrom (MT Rezon), and Hadrazar (MT Hadadezer). "The one in Raemmaer" reflects a Greek transliteration of Hebrew "who fled from," leaving "Hadrazar king of Zobah, his lord" syntactically loose in the Greek.
notes.11:19: Greek preserves the distinct name Thekemina (MT Tahpenes); likewise, in 11:26, 11:43, and 12:24 Greek reads Sareira (MT Zeredah).
notes.11:34: Greek reads "I will surely oppose him" (antitassomenos antitaxomai auto) where MT reads "I will make him prince"; similarly in 11:36 Greek reads thesis ("a position") where MT has "a lamp."
notes.12:10: "My littleness" translates Greek he mikrotes mou literally (also in 12:24), a euphemistic idiom traditionally understood as "my little finger."
notes.12:18: Greek reads the distinct name Aram (MT Adoram) and omits "into his chariot"; verses 2 and 17 are absent in the LXX (the material of MT 12:2 appears in 11:43).
notes.12:20: The Greek text reads "Rehoboam" here (where MT has "Jeroboam") and adds "and Benjamin" to the tribe following David; in 12:21 Greek reads "one hundred and twenty thousand" (MT 180,000).
notes.12:24: The LXX includes a long alternate account of Rehoboam's accession and Jeroboam's rise (often numbered 12:24a-z), featuring distinct numbers (Rehoboam aged sixteen, reigning twelve years), distinct names (Naanan, Ana, Sareisa, Ano, Thekemina, Enlamite), and Shemaiah performing the twelve-piece garment sign.
notes.12:27: Greek reads "to the Lord and to their lord" (pros Kyrion kai kyrion auton, where MT has only "to their lord"); in 12:28 and 12:32 Greek uses feminine damalis ("heifers") where MT has "calves."
notes.13:3: The Greek reads future 'he will give' (literally rendering a Hebrew waw-perfect) even though v. 5 refers to the portent as already given by the man of God. It also reads 'word' (rather than 'sign') and 'fatness' (literally rendering the Hebrew term for fat-soaked altar ashes).
notes.13:6: The Greek uses an active transitive verb ('brought the king's hand back') with an implicit subject, most naturally the Lord answering the plea (though grammatically it could continue 'the man of God'), where the Hebrew reads intransitively ('the king's hand returned').
notes.13:11: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'and they told them to their father,' the Greek reads 'and they turned the face of their father.'
notes.13:26: The Greek text lacks the second half of v. 26 (concerning the Lord handing the prophet over to the lion) and all of v. 27 found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.13:33: 'Fill his hand' is a literal biblical idiom for consecrating or ordaining someone to the priesthood.
notes.14:21: Verses 14:1-20 are absent at this position in the Greek text (parallel material appears in the Greek supplement after 12:24). The Greek names Rehoboam's mother Maacham, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Naamah.
notes.14:24: The Greek reads 'a conspiracy' (syndesmos), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's reference to cult prostitutes.
notes.14:26: The Greek adds the reference to the golden spears that David took from the servants of Hadarezer king of Zobah (cf. 2 Samuel 8:7) and refers to 'golden weapons' (hopla, a term also used for shields), omitting the Hebrew reference to golden shields made by Solomon.
notes.14:27: The Greek reads 'the leaders of the runners ... set upon him,' differing sharply from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ('he entrusted them to the commanders of the guards').
notes.14:31: The Greek reads Abiou (corresponding to Hebrew Abiyahu/Abijah, as in 2 Chronicles 13:20), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text of 1 Kings reads Abijam; the Greek also omits the repeated mention of Rehoboam's mother here.
notes.15:1: Greek reads "Abiu son of Jeroboam" (and "six years" in 15:2, omitting 15:6 and 15:32), where the Hebrew text has "Abijam" son of Rehoboam reigning three years.
notes.15:13: Here and in 15:10, Greek names Asa's mother "Ana" (Hebrew: Maacah), describes an "assembly in her grove" and "hiding places" (Hebrew: an abominable image for Asherah), and renders Hebrew "Kidron" literally as "of the cedars."
notes.15:18: Greek mentions only the royal treasuries (omitting the Lord's house) and renders the Syrian royal lineage as "the son of Hader, son of Taberema, son of Hazin" (Hebrew: Ben-hadad, Tabrimmon, Hezion); in 15:20 Greek similarly reads "Ain," "Adelmath," and "Chezrath" (Hebrew: Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Chinneroth).
notes.15:22: Greek transliterates the Hebrew phrase "none was exempt" as a place name ("to Ainakim") and translates the place names Geba and Mizpah as common nouns ("every hill of Benjamin and the watchtower").
notes.15:25: Here and in 15:27, 31, Greek names Jeroboam's son "Nebat" (Nabath/Nabat, identical to Jeroboam's father) where the Hebrew has "Nadab"; in 15:27 Greek also reads "house of Belaan" (Hebrew: house of Issachar) and an unusual verb (literally "gashed/cut") rendered "wounded."
notes.16:6: Greek dates Elah's accession here to Asa's twentieth year (Hebrew places it in Asa's twenty-sixth year in 16:8), and in 16:9 names the steward "Osa" (Hebrew: Arza).
notes.16:15: Greek states that Zimri reigned "seven years" in Tirzah while Israel's camp was at "Gibeon" (Hebrew: "seven days" and "Gibbethon").
notes.16:16: From 16:16 through 16:29, this Greek text consistently reads "Zimri" where the Hebrew distinguishes "Omri" from Zimri; in 16:18 it also reads "into a cave" and "the king burned," and in 16:22 adds "and Joram his brother."
notes.16:28: Greek places the entire summary of Jehoshaphat's reign here (corresponding to Hebrew 1 Kings 22:41-50), dating it to Zimri's eleventh year, naming his mother "Gabuza" (Hebrew: Azubah), reading "Syria" (Hebrew: Edom) and "Sophir" (Hebrew: Ophir), and transliterating the Hebrew word for "deputy" as "nasib."
notes.16:33: Greek reads "grove" (Hebrew: Asherah) and "to provoke his own soul to anger, so as to be utterly destroyed," where the Hebrew reads "to provoke the Lord, the God of Israel, to anger."
notes.17:1: The Greek adds "the prophet," reads "from Tishbe of Gilead" (vs. Hebrew MT "of the settlers of Gilead"), and includes "the God of powers" (Greek: ton dynameon, corresponding to Hebrew "of hosts"); the closing phrase literally reads "except through the mouth of my word."
notes.17:6: Unlike the Hebrew MT ("bread and meat in the morning and bread and meat in the evening"), the Greek specifies loaves of bread in the morning and meat in the evening.
notes.17:12: Here and in vv. 13 and 15, the Greek reads the plural "children" where the Hebrew MT has the singular "son."
notes.17:20: The Greek addresses the Lord as "the witness of the widow" (reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew) and states Elijah's lament as a direct declaration rather than a question.
notes.17:21: The Greek reads "breathed upon the boy three times" (vs. Hebrew MT "stretched himself upon the child three times"), and v. 22 gives the shorter Greek report ("And it happened so, and the boy cried out").
notes.18:10: The Greek reads "he burned down the kingdom and its regions" where the Hebrew MT reads "he made the kingdom or nation swear"; similarly in v. 5 the Greek reads "from the tents" (vs. MT "of the animals").
notes.18:19: Here and in v. 25 the Greek replaces the name Baal with "shame" ("prophets of shame"), and renders Asherah as "the groves" (singular "the grove" in v. 22); in v. 29 the Greek adds Elijah's command to "the prophets of the abominations" to step aside.
